card.statement:
We have allowed $\mathbf{n}$ to be a multiple of the order $\mathbf{n}^{\prime}$ of the automorphism $a$ , rather than requiring $\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{n}^{\prime}$ . This does not create any substantially new examples of split-quotient quivers, since it follows easily from the definition that $(\widetilde{I},\widetilde{H},\widetilde{\Omega})$ is the disconnected union of $\mathbf{n}/\mathbf{n}^{\prime}$ copies of the split-quotient quiver defined using $\mathbf{n}^{\prime}$ instead of $\mathbf{n}$ . In particular, if $a$ is the identity automorphism, $(\widetilde{I},\widetilde{H},\widetilde{\Omega})$ is the disconnected union of $\mathbf{n}$ copies of $(I,H,\Omega)$ .

2.3. Interpretation via the McKay correspondence

Recall the McKay correspondence [Mc] between simply-laced affine Dynkin diagrams and conjugacy classes of nontrivial finite subgroups $\Gamma$ of $SL_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ , in which the vertices of the diagram $\widetilde{\Delta}_{\Gamma}$ label the isomorphism classes of irreducible representations of $\Gamma$ . Slodowy observed [Sl, Section 6.2, Appendix III] that certain automorphisms of affine Dynkin diagrams arise from pairs $(\Gamma,\Gamma^{\prime})$ of such groups where $\Gamma\subsetneq\Gamma^{\prime}$ , $\Gamma$ is normal in $\Gamma^{\prime}$ , the quotient $\Gamma^{\prime}/\Gamma$ is cyclic of order $\mathbf{n}$ and the centralizer of $\Gamma$ in $\Gamma^{\prime}$ is contained in $\Gamma$ . (This characterization of the relevant pairs is from [Lu4, Section 2].) Explicitly, given such a pair $(\Gamma,\Gamma^{\prime})$ :

(1)

the conjugation action of a generator of $\Gamma^{\prime}/\Gamma$ on irreducible representations of $\Gamma$ defines an order- $\mathbf{n}$ automorphism $a$ of $\widetilde{\Delta}_{\Gamma}$ , and

(2)

tensoring irreducible representations of $\Gamma^{\prime}$ with a generator of $\widehat{\Gamma^{\prime}/\Gamma}$ (thought of as a linear character of $\Gamma^{\prime}$ ) defines an order- $\mathbf{n}$ automorphism $a^{\prime}$ of $\widetilde{\Delta}_{\Gamma^{\prime}}$ .

By inspection of the various cases, automorphisms arising in either of these two ways are admissible (and $\mathbf{n}$ is always either $2$ or $3$ ). The nontrivial admissible automorphisms of simply-laced affine Dynkin diagrams that do not arise thus are the ‘rotations’ of $\widetilde{\mathrm{A}}_{m}$ and the order- $4$ automorphisms of $\widetilde{\mathrm{D}}_{2m}$ .

paper.title: Diagram automorphisms of quiver varieties
paper.abstract: We show that the fixed-point subvariety of a Nakajima quiver variety under a diagram automorphism is a disconnected union of quiver varieties for the `split-quotient quiver' introduced by Reiten and Riedtmann. As a special case, quiver varieties of type D arise as the connected components of fixed-point subvarieties of diagram involutions of quiver varieties of type A. In the case where the quiver varieties of type A correspond to small self-dual representations, we show that the diagram involutions coincide with classical involutions of two-row Slodowy varieties. It follows that certain quiver varieties of type D are isomorphic to Slodowy varieties for orthogonal or symplectic Lie algebras.
